capabilities: Provide a Neovim-compatible Vim editing engine with Markdown text objects, motions, surround, and folding
Configure behavior with Lua (.obsidian.init.lua) and a built-in vimrc loader with hot-reload
Jump within and across notes using flash/EasyMotion labels, marks, and a cross-note jump list
Manage files, tables, headings, and workspace panes with Vim commands and keyboard navigation
Optionally delegate editing to a user-supplied Neovim 0.12+ binary over msgpack-RPC
disambiguation: Not just motion keybindings; it is a full Vim engine with Lua configuration, a file explorer, a fuzzy picker, snippets, and an optional external Neovim backend.
extras: The README requires disabling Obsidian's built-in Vim mode. RPC mode runs the user's Neovim binary and config as arbitrary code with no sandbox. Several features (Neovim backend, external grep, IM switching, vim in text areas, reveal table mode) are desktop-only or experimental; the raw table mode is deprecated. Full documentation lives on an external site.
intentEvidence: Vim Motions adds what's missing from Obsidian's built-in Vim mode: Markdown-aware text objects, structural navigation
problem: Obsidian's built-in Vim mode lacks Markdown-aware text objects, Lua scripting, and most Neovim features, limiting keyboard-driven editing.

relations.evidence: Vim Motions provides its own enhanced vim engine — a fork of codemirror-vim
Flash motions — enhanced f/F/t/T with labels on all visible matches (flash.nvim-inspired)

add, change, or delete surrounding delimiters (vim-surround with Markdown support

summary: Neovim-style Vim engine for Obsidian with Markdown text objects, Lua configuration, EasyMotion jumps, surround, folding, and an optional external Neovim backend.
